seo.title: Optimization Engine | Fintela
seo.description: Seven search algorithms, how to pick the right one, and the engine that runs them in parallel, recovers from failures, and swaps your sampler for a grid when the space is finite.

samplers.title: Seven ways to explore
samplers.description: The sampler is the algorithm that decides which parameter combination a study's next trial tries. Five classic algorithms, plus two experimental ones that run on a simulated quantum computer, all coordinated by the same optimization engine that scales, recovers from failures, and keeps your study running.

algorithms.title: The same field, seven ways to search it

tpe.title: TPE
tpe.desc: Learns from the trials already run: it models the "good" and "bad" results as two separate densities, and proposes points more likely under the good one. Fintela's default, and the right choice for most searches, especially on modest budgets, since it gets useful signal from relatively few trials.

bullets.label: Full name
bullets.desc: Tree-structured Parzen Estimator.

bullets.label: Best for
bullets.desc: General purpose, mixed parameter types.

bullets.label: Parallelism
bullets.desc: Runs across multiple workers; adjusts itself so they don't propose near-identical combinations at once.

bullets.label: Recommended budget
bullets.desc: 100 to 1,000 trials.

cmaEs.title: CMA-ES
cmaEs.desc: Evolves a population of candidates, adapting the mean and covariance of a multivariate Gaussian toward the best-performing regions each generation. Works best with continuous parameters and a large trial budget.

bullets.label: Full name
bullets.desc: Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy.

bullets.label: Best for
bullets.desc: High parallelism, continuous parameters.

bullets.label: Parallelism
bullets.desc: Runs across multiple workers in parallel.

bullets.label: Recommended budget
bullets.desc: 1,000 to 10,000 trials.

nsga2.title: NSGA-II
nsga2.desc: A population-based genetic algorithm: instead of proposing one combination at a time, it evaluates a whole batch together, which makes it naturally suited to running many trials in parallel. Fintela always runs it against a single objective, even though algorithms like this are often used for multi-objective optimization elsewhere.

bullets.label: Full name
bullets.desc: Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II.

bullets.label: Best for
bullets.desc: Large budgets, many categorical or discrete parameters.

bullets.label: Parallelism
bullets.desc: Runs across multiple workers; batch size adjusts automatically.

bullets.label: Recommended budget
bullets.desc: 100 to 10,000 trials.

qmc.title: QMC
qmc.desc: Uses a low-discrepancy sequence instead of pure randomness, spreading trials more evenly across the search space. Useful for sensitivity sweeps, or an early pass before committing a larger budget to a smarter sampler.

bullets.label: Full name
bullets.desc: Quasi-Monte Carlo.

bullets.label: Best for
bullets.desc: Systematic coverage, or a step up from a baseline.

bullets.label: Parallelism
bullets.desc: Runs across multiple workers, no coordination needed.

bullets.label: Recommended budget
bullets.desc: Unlimited.

random.title: Random
random.desc: Pure uniform random sampling, with no memory of past trials. Scales to any number of parallel workers with no coordination overhead: the honest baseline any smarter sampler should beat.

bullets.label: Full name
bullets.desc: Random Search.

bullets.label: Best for
bullets.desc: A control baseline, or very large search spaces.

bullets.label: Parallelism
bullets.desc: Runs across multiple workers, no coordination needed.

bullets.label: Recommended budget
bullets.desc: Unlimited.

qaoa.title: QAOA
qaoa.desc: Experimental: proposes each combination using a simulated quantum circuit instead of classical statistics. Emulated in software: no real quantum hardware involved, and no current speed advantage over the classical samplers. Starts with random trials while it warms up, and falls back to random sampling if anything fails or the space is too large.

bullets.label: Full name
bullets.desc: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (emulated).

bullets.label: Best for
bullets.desc: Experimenting with quantum-inspired search.

bullets.label: Parallelism
bullets.desc: Runs on a single worker, since it keeps an internal model that can't be split.

bullets.label: Recommended budget
bullets.desc: 50 to 500 trials.

qKernel.title: Q-Kernel
qKernel.desc: Also experimental: intelligent optimization in the spirit of TPE, but its similarity model is computed with a simulated quantum feature map instead of a classical kernel. Shares QAOA's random warmup and automatic fallback.

bullets.label: Full name
bullets.desc: Quantum Kernel Intelligent Optimization (emulated).

bullets.label: Best for
bullets.desc: Experimenting with a simulated quantum similarity kernel.

bullets.label: Parallelism
bullets.desc: Runs on a single worker.

bullets.label: Recommended budget
bullets.desc: 30 to 300 trials.

picking.title: A quick guide for your situation

unsure.label: Not sure?
unsure.value: Start with TPE: the default, and the right choice for most searches.

continuous.label: All continuous, big budget, many workers

coverage.label: Even coverage, or a sensitivity sweep

quantum.label: Want to experiment with quantum search

engine.title: What actually happens when you launch a study
engine.description: The sampler decides what to try; the optimization engine decides how to run it: how many workers, in what order, and what to do when something goes wrong.

automaticScaling.title: Automatic worker scaling
automaticScaling.desc: Fintela decides how many workers your study needs, with nothing for you to configure.

bullets.label: Bigger budget, more workers
bullets.desc: a 20-trial study doesn't get the same compute as a 2,000-trial one.

bullets.label: External strategies and fitness functions
bullets.desc: collapse the study to a single worker, respecting the concurrency limit you declared.

bullets.label: Automatic retry
bullets.desc: if a worker runs out of memory, Fintela retries with a larger allocation, up to three times, without charging you again for what already ran.

batchPipeline.title: Pipelined batches, not trial by trial
batchPipeline.desc: Trials move in batches, and while one is being saved, the next is already being simulated.

bullets.label: Data processed once per batch
bullets.desc: not once per trial, so nothing is redone.

bullets.label: Saved immediately
bullets.desc: each finished batch saves right away; you never see a half-finished study.

bullets.label: Isolation
bullets.desc: if one trial fails, only that one fails; the rest of the batch and the study continue.

finiteGrid.title: Finite grids replace your sampler
finiteGrid.desc: If your search space is small enough to enumerate completely, Fintela detects it before your study launches.

bullets.label: Up to 1,000,000 combinations
bullets.desc: Fintela automatically switches to a grid search: every combination tried exactly once.

bullets.label: Your sampler simply doesn't apply then
bullets.desc: except QAOA and Q-Kernel, which are exempt and keep their normal behavior.

bullets.label: The builder warns you
bullets.desc: with the exact size of the space, before you spend any tokens.

failureRecovery.title: Automatic failure recovery
failureRecovery.desc: A study doesn't go down over one trial, one worker, or a memory spike.

bullets.label: Per-trial isolation
bullets.desc: an error in one trial doesn't affect the rest of the batch or the study.

bullets.label: Early auto-stop
bullets.desc: if too many trials fail, the study stops itself before it keeps spending your budget.

bullets.label: Everything finished stays
bullets.desc: resuming or relaunching a partial study only computes what's left, not from scratch.

bullets.label: Automatic refund
bullets.desc: Fintela compares what you were charged at launch against the actual cost, and refunds the difference.

liveProgress.title: Live progress and health
liveProgress.desc: Nothing is pushed to you trial by trial: the app keeps itself current by checking in on the study for you.

bullets.label: About every 5 seconds
bullets.desc: while the study is active, the status, progress, and health indicators update.

bullets.label: Progress and Health
bullets.desc: what share of your budget has resolved, and what share of that succeeded.

bullets.label: Never a stale snapshot
bullets.desc: the progress you see always reflects the live number, not a minute-old picture.

sameEngine.title: The same engine, from sandbox to full study
sameEngine.desc: The simulation engine behind a single sandbox backtest is exactly the same one that runs every trial inside a full study.

bullets.label: No surprises
bullets.desc: a strategy that behaves a certain way in a quick test behaves the same inside a study; the only difference is how many combinations get tried.

bullets.label: Risk managers evaluated per simulated day
bullets.desc: inside each trial, not once per trial.

bullets.label: External code, same rules
bullets.desc: Fintela retries automatically on connection failures, never on an endpoint that's simply slow.

limits.title: The limits, with no fine print

noMultiObjective.label: No multi-objective search
noMultiObjective.value: Every study optimizes a single objective. To balance two goals, build the tradeoff into one custom fitness function.

noSeed.label: No seed
noSeed.value: There's no reproducibility setting: TPE, CMA-ES, Random, QMC, and NSGA-II each explore a different trial sequence on every run.

samplerLocked.label: The sampler locks in at launch
samplerLocked.value: You can only change it while the study is still a draft; duplicate the study to try a different one.

noWorkerControl.label: No manual worker control
noWorkerControl.value: How many workers run your study is decided automatically by Fintela, based on your execution type, sampler, and trial budget.

samplers.note: These are general descriptions of each algorithm family, meant as guidance, not an exact specification of Fintela's implementation.

connect.title: One key, one HTTP client, zero setup

key.label: Personal key

openapi.label: Always-current reference
openapi.value: A full OpenAPI specification, generated from the live API, so standard tools can generate client code in your language.

responses.label: Consistent responses
responses.value: Every response shares the same envelope; errors come with a clear message and a machine-checkable code, and every call carries an id support can trace.

scoped.label: Only yours
scoped.value: The key reads exactly what your organization sees in the app. A resource from another org responds the same as one that doesn't exist.

rateLimit.label: A generous limit
rateLimit.value: Around 20 sustained requests per second per organization, with bursts up to 40. If you go over, the response tells you how long to wait.

noPush.label: No push
noPush.value: No webhooks or streams: poll at whatever interval makes sense. Most lists come back newest first, so checking the top is usually enough.

plan.label: A plan feature
plan.value: The Developer API is turned on for your organization like any other premium capability.

engine.description: A quick sandbox run, the thousands of trials in a study, a promoted portfolio's daily extension, and a Trading Lab what-if all come out of the same engine, with the same rules: the engine the API exposes.

oneEngine.title: One engine for everything
oneEngine.desc: The sandbox, every study trial, and a live portfolio's daily extension are all computed with the same logic.

bullets.label: The same engine everywhere
bullets.desc: what you see in a quick test is exactly what you'll see inside a study.

bullets.label: A backtest is a record
bullets.desc: every study freezes the engine version, cost rate, and benchmark it launched with.

bullets.label: Multi-asset
bullets.desc: US equities, ETFs, indices, crypto, FX, and global markets, in the same engine and the same universe.

howItSimulates.title: How it simulates
howItSimulates.desc: A daily rebalance, with the data the strategy asks for and guardrails evaluated inside the loop.

bullets.label: Daily rebalance
bullets.desc: the strategy hands back a signal and the engine executes it at adjusted closing prices.

bullets.label: Data the engine delivers
bullets.desc: prices always, plus volume, fundamentals, indicators, or sector when the strategy selects them.

bullets.label: Risk managers inside the loop
bullets.desc: evaluated every simulated day, before the rebalance: a real guardrail, not an after-the-fact filter.

bullets.label: A portfolio of portfolios
bullets.desc: your own portfolio groups can enter the universe as just another asset.

bullets.label: Isolation
bullets.desc: if one trial fails, only that one fails; the rest of the batch keeps going.

transactionCosts.title: Realistic transaction costs
transactionCosts.desc: Every trade pays, so the optimizer learns to actually win, not just to trade for free.

bullets.label: Every trade pays
bullets.desc: 10 bps on US equities, 30 bps on crypto, 5 bps on FX; a mixed universe pays the highest rate.

bullets.label: Cost-free, if you ask for it
bullets.desc: run a frictionless study to measure how much of the result is the cost model.

bullets.label: Both versions, side by side
bullets.desc: a promoted portfolio or portfolio group can be read under the other regime: a full twin simulation.

antiOverfitting.title: Built against overfitting
antiOverfitting.desc: Three separate periods and an automatic statistical verdict, so the out-of-sample result is judged exactly once.

bullets.label: Three separate periods
bullets.desc: the optimizer only ever sees train; validation is reported but never influences the search; out-of-sample is derived server-side, strictly after validation.

bullets.label: Real-life performance
bullets.desc: a fourth period that only tells time: what the portfolio does once promoted, updated every day.

bullets.label: Automatic verdict
bullets.desc: Well Trained · Borderline · Overfit Risk · Insufficient Data, based on Probabilistic and Deflated Sharpe, PBO, and train/validation-to-OOS degradation.

bullets.label: Skill vs. luck
bullets.desc: the Sharpe the best trial would reach by pure luck; your result has to beat it to count as a real edge.

bullets.label: Strategy families
bullets.desc: groups trials by their equity curve and tells you how many are genuinely distinct.

backtestOutput.title: What every backtest produces
backtestOutput.desc: An equity curve, 35 metrics, and the full detail behind every number.

bullets.label: Equity curve
bullets.desc: day by day, across every period, with and without a benchmark.

bullets.label: 35 metrics
bullets.desc: 26 portfolio metrics (Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, drawdowns, VaR/CVaR…) and 9 benchmark-relative ones (alpha, beta, information ratio…).

bullets.label: By period and by window
bullets.desc: every metric across train / validation / OOS / real-life, and across 9 rolling windows.

bullets.label: Holdings, trades, and risk
bullets.desc: what was held each day, every closed trade, drawdowns, and the risk manager's log.

bullets.label: Downloadable seed
bullets.desc: the exact signal the strategy produced each day, in JSON or CSV.

askAgain.title: Ask the engine again
askAgain.desc: Sandbox, what-if, and the Trading Lab: the same engine, without spending a new study.

bullets.label: Sandbox
bullets.desc: test a strategy, fitness function, or risk manager in a single backtest, before spending a study.

bullets.label: Instant what-if
bullets.desc: invert the signal, shorten the window, exclude names; the engine re-simulates and shows the exact delta. It's never saved.

bullets.label: Trading Lab and Ideas
bullets.desc: try a different rebalance cadence, allocation method, or excluding the worst detractor, with one click.

bullets.label: Group track record
bullets.desc: a portfolio group's combined curve already includes the cost of rebalancing between members.

scale.title: Scales without you configuring it
scale.desc: Automatic parallelism, failure recovery, and seven search algorithms.

bullets.label: Automatic parallelism
bullets.desc: a study is split across workers, with multiple trials running at once inside each; nothing to configure.

bullets.label: Results as they arrive
bullets.desc: each finished batch is saved to your study immediately, complete or not saved at all: you never see a half-finished study.

bullets.label: Automatic recovery
bullets.desc: a trial that runs out of memory is retried, an interrupted batch runs once more, a crashed worker never loses what was already saved.

bullets.label: Seven search algorithms
bullets.desc: TPE (default), CMA-ES, NSGA-II (multi-objective), QMC, Random, and two research samplers with quantum emulation (QAOA and Q-Kernel).

bullets.label: Autostop, pause, and resume
bullets.desc: stop a study whenever you want and resume it later with more trials, without losing what's done.

yourCode.title: Your code, inside or outside
yourCode.desc: Python in Fintela's own editor, or your own server: the engine calls the logic the same way either way.

bullets.label: Internal
bullets.desc: you write the strategy, fitness, or risk manager in Python (or Fintelligent drafts it) and the engine runs it.

bullets.label: External
bullets.desc: the logic lives on your own server; Fintela never sees or stores your code, with automatic retries and a concurrency limit you set.

bullets.label: Validated before it saves
bullets.desc: all internal code is compiled and tested against real data before it can be saved; errors show up in seconds, not mid-study.

toLive.title: From backtest to live, without switching engines
toLive.desc: A promoted trial keeps extending every day with the same engine and the same costs.

bullets.label: Promotion
bullets.desc: a trial becomes a managed portfolio, which stops moving with the study and extends every day with new market data.

bullets.label: Live operation
bullets.desc: a portfolio group bundles managed portfolios and trades on a broker, paper or real.

bullets.label: Daily reconciliation
bullets.desc: between what Fintela computes and what the broker reports.

fintelaApi.closingLine: A Fintela backtest isn't a pretty curve: it's a daily simulation with real costs, guardrails inside the loop, and a statistical verdict on whether the result is luck or skill: available in your own tools with a key and an HTTP client.
fintelaApi.note: Read-only: nothing sent through this channel can create, modify, or delete anything. Every response follows the same standard format, authenticated with a personal access key.
